tldr: Joint intervention laws retain dependence between outcome coordinates and distinguish a zero state from positive responses. In the supplied bivariate benchmark, the continuous square can meet the origin atom as the public gap closes. The research object is the exact minimax integrated squared-\(W_2\) precision for both conditional laws, including every logarithm and gap transition. A corner-release transport comparison, observable local counts and a same-class information converse provide the starting handles. The numerical frontier and attaining finite rule are derivation outputs. A boundary corollary distinguishes quadratic logarithmic contact from linear mass-transfer cost at a fixed positive gap. A common-submodel comparison isolates the continuous-reconstruction certificate when the atom weights are publicly fixed.
gap: Positive-density transport comparisons and separated-support mass floors leave the planar atom-contact precision cost unresolved for the supplied conditional mixed class. The bounded literature audit found no verified theorem giving its complete all-gap risk certificate.
fill: The kernel determines one explicit numerical order for \(R(n,g)\), a total original-record attaining rule, and a matching converse over exactly \(\mathcal M_g\). The geometric step must handle atom imbalance and continuous-density errors together with constants uniform at contact. The contact-boundary corollary identifies the geometric regimes. A strict upper-certificate comparison on the constant-atom submodel credits positive-density conditional smoothing without changing the full-class criterion.
